clue.text: Free ranger in Providence?

parts.note: a free-range hen breed named after the US state whose capital is Providence

explanation.surface: Someone roaming freely about a city, or perhaps about divine providence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ranger' looks like a park warden, but a free ranger is a free-range chicken, and Providence is the capital of the smallest US state, which gave its name to a famous breed of hen.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is a reddish domestic chicken developed in that New England state and often kept free range.

clue.text: Hospital to improve image — it should make Barnet more attractive

definitions.text: it should make Barnet more attractive

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
to airbrush a photo is to retouch it so it looks better

explanation.surface: A hospital touching up its public image, with a London borough thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is a London borough, but in Cockney rhyming slang 'Barnet Fair' means hair, so a Barnet is a head of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A grooming tool with bristles is used to tidy the hair, making one's locks look better.

clue.text: Detectives went north to seize gold order

indicators.note: seizing means the reversed detectives grab and hold the gold within them
in a down clue, going north means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Police heading north to make a seizure of gold on orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command, but it is a style of classical architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the classical architectural styles of column, alongside Ionic and Corinthian.

clue.text: Nose reconstruction in subcontinent or somewhere further east

indicators.note: in means the rebuilt letters go inside the subcontinent's name

parts.note: India is the country commonly called the subcontinent

indicators.note: a reconstruction rebuilds the nose, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone choosing where to have cosmetic nose surgery: India or a place further east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reconstruction' looks like surgery, but it signals the anagram; 'or' is just a link between the two places.
explanation.definitionFit: The Southeast Asian archipelago nation lies east of India across the Bay of Bengal.

clue.text: Survives uprising in Lebanese village

indicators.note: uprising says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters lie buried inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A village in Lebanon living through a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' unexplained: it signals the hidden letters, which 'uprising' then reads from the bottom up in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To survive is to go on existing, to stay alive, the plain verb sense.

clue.text: Longing to be lost again at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor yearning to be adrift and lost on the ocean again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' looks like part of the sailor's picture but signals the shuffle of LOST AGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sentimental yearning for the past, a wistful longing for times gone by.

clue.text: Native Australians take time to settle

parts.note: roos, short for kangaroos, are animals native to Australia

explanation.surface: Aboriginal Australians taking their time to put down roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native Australians' suggests people, but here they are kangaroos.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds settle on a perch for the night, which is the verb sense of the word.

clue.text: Rescind incorrect notice

indicators.note: incorrect means wrongly arranged, so the letters of rescind are shuffled

explanation.surface: An official withdrawing a notice that was posted in error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a noun, a posted sign, but it is the verb meaning perceive.
explanation.definitionFit: To perceive or make out something, to spot it, is the verb sense meant here.

clue.text: Odds are about snow initially being thin on the ground

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds when a race begins

indicators.note: about means the word are goes around the snow's first letter
initially says take only the first letter of snow

explanation.surface: A bookmaker quoting odds on whether there will be any snow on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thin on the ground' plays off the snow picture but simply means scarce.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce, scattered and few in number is thin on the ground, an idiom for scanty.

clue.text: Earlier advertising about Olympic venue

indicators.note: about means the advertising letters wrap around the venue

parts.note: PR, public relations, is publicity work akin to advertising
Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Summer Olympics

explanation.surface: A recollection of earlier promotional work around the Olympic Games host city.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming before in time, previous or preceding, is the adjective sense meant.

clue.text: Differences of opinion in leagues

definitions.meaning: sports leagues are split into tiers, such as the first and second

explanation.surface: Disagreements arising within sporting competitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a split between factions and a ranked tier of a football league.

clue.text: Point of no return for Polish idol

parts.note: to polish something is to rub it
an icon is a revered figure, an idol

explanation.surface: A Polish pop star reaching a point from which there is no going back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality; lower-case it is the verb meaning rub.
explanation.definitionFit: The river Caesar crossed in 49 BC, committing to civil war, stands for an irrevocable step.

clue.text: Latte brewed in extremely suave city

indicators.note: in means the reworked letters sit between the outer letters of suave
extremely means take only the letters at the very ends of suave
a brewed drink is made up afresh, so the letters of latte are reworked

explanation.surface: A smooth coffee brewed in a famously coffee-mad city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives just the outer letters S and E of 'suave'; 'brewed' signals the anagram that sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the largest city in Washington state, on Puget Sound, known for its coffee culture.

clue.text: Provide on-line joke?

parts.note: E is the prefix for electronic, as in e-mail, so it stands for online
a quip is a witty remark or joke

explanation.surface: Is this an internet meme, a joke shared online?
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish someone with the necessary items, to supply them, is the verb sense.

clue.text: Military jumper left metropolis flipping drunk

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier who jumps from aircraft

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so the city's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a metropolis is a large city

explanation.surface: A paratrooper leaves the big city in a drunken rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' poses as a mild British curse word ('flipping drunk') but signals the reversal YTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for extremely intoxicated, so drunk one can barely move.

clue.text: Foolishly reneges about silver colour

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the silver
foolishly means done in a silly, muddled way, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly going back on a deal over silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foolishly' gives SEGREEN; 'about' puts it around the silver, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft greyish-green shade, named after the leaves of the culinary herb.

clue.text: Unusual foresight — avoid an oral examination here

definitions.note: a plural instruction: avoid inspecting this present's mouth

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Remarkable foresight means skipping a spoken exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says never look this in the mouth: checking a horse's teeth reveals its age, rude when it is a present. 'Oral examination' sounds like a viva, but it is a look in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially, a present should be accepted without inspecting its teeth for faults.

clue.text: Vehicle, say, in hurry up …

indicators.note: in means the word for say goes inside the reversed hurry
in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to race is to hurry
to state is to say

explanation.surface: Someone telling a car to get a move on, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hurry up' looks like an order but splits: in a down clue 'up' gives ECAR, and 'in' puts the word for say inside it after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: A British term for a car with a long body and rear door, what Americans call a station wagon.

clue.text: Poor health for partner

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A spouse falling ill, as in sickness and in health.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an idiom for one's spouse or long-term partner, the other part of a couple.

clue.text: … only to be caught by zero credit for a month

parts.note: O looks like the digit zero

indicators.note: caught by means the words to be are held inside the credit letters

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: Continuing the car's rush, only to be caught out by a lack of credit.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the previous clue's surface; 'only' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth month of the year, falling between September and November.

clue.text: Both genders abandoned criminal player

indicators.note: abandoned means these letters are dropped and left behind

parts.note: a malefactor is a wrongdoer or criminal
MALE spelt out plus F, the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A criminal deserted by both men and women alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both genders' gives MALE in full and F for female, removed from the front of MALEFACTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer in a play is a player, the theatrical sense of the word.

clue.text: Worry when Twitter fails to open

indicators.note: fails to open means the first letter goes missing

parts.note: twitter is idle chatter, prattle

explanation.surface: Anxiety when the social media app will not load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twitter' looks like the social network, but here it is chatter, PRATTLE, losing its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle or fluster someone, making them nervous, is the verb sense meant.

clue.text: Dogged pedant finally complained bitterly

indicators.note: finally means take only the last letter of pedant

parts.note: to rail is to protest angrily

explanation.surface: A persistent pedant finally ranted in bitter complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogged' looks like an adjective, stubborn, but it is the verb, followed.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow someone closely, as a hound does, is to dog or track them.

clue.text: Tired of wrestling?

definitions.meaning: a freestyle wrestling style with few holds barred

explanation.surface: Weary of the sport of grappling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means exhausted and also names a no-holds-barred form of wrestling.

clue.text: Peg would be advised to finish early

indicators.note: finish early means the last letter is cut off before the end

parts.note: you would be advised to do something means you would do well to do it

explanation.surface: Advice to a man named Peg that he should knock off work early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peg' looks like a woman's name but is a wooden pin.
explanation.definitionFit: A short wooden rod used as a pin to join pieces of furniture is a kind of peg.

clue.text: Practice at home

parts.note: a habit is a regular practice

explanation.surface: Practising something in the comfort of one's own house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At home' reads as a phrase, but 'at' is wordplay and 'home' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The natural surroundings where an animal or plant lives are its home.

clue.text: Grouse featuring in reputable attraction

indicators.note: featuring in means the answer appears within the run of these words

explanation.surface: A game bird appearing as the star of a respectable tourist draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' looks like the game bird but is the verb, complain.
explanation.definitionFit: To grumble or moan is to complain, as a sheep's plaintive cry suggests.

clue.text: Barker carries the first on The Belfry

indicators.note: carries means the bellower holds a letter inside

parts.note: a bellower is one who barks or shouts loudly

indicators.note: the first on means take only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A dog carrying the leader onto a famous golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: The Belfry is an English golf venue that has hosted the Ryder Cup, but 'Belfry' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A belfry is the tower or part of a steeple where bells hang.

clue.text: Outperform forty in audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the letters are spoken aloud

parts.note: XL is forty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Forty actors trying to outshine each other at a tryout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audition' looks like a casting session but here means hearing: XL said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To do better than others, to surpass them, is to outperform.

clue.text: They are sent by letter to demand payment

definitions.text: They are sent by letter to demand payment

parts.words: They are sent by letter to demand payment
parts.note: a letter here is one who lets property, a landlord, who dispatches agents to collect what tenants owe

explanation.surface: Debt demands posted to people by mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like mail but means one who lets out property: a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: Agents sent by landlords to gather tenants' periodic payments for housing.
